section_name: Foundational Statistical Prediction and Residual Mean Intercept Explanation

candidates.title: Leverage and Regression Through the Origin
candidates.reason: Seminal pedagogical paper examining linear models without an intercept versus models with an intercept, rigorously analyzing how forcing a zero intercept alters residual behavior, violates the zero-sum residual property, and distorts model leverage.

candidates.title: Regression through the Origin
candidates.reason: Foundational teaching reference explaining the mathematical derivation of ordinary least squares without an intercept, illustrating how omitting a constant term leaves non-zero residual sums and biases baseline predictions.

candidates.title: Fitting Regression Models with No Intercept Term
candidates.reason: Classic methodological guide detailing the consequences of fitting straight lines without an intercept term, explicitly demonstrating that residuals do not average to zero when a non-zero constant offset is omitted.

candidates.title: Cautionary Note about R2
candidates.reason: Highly cited foundational paper in The American Statistician demonstrating that omitting the intercept term invalidates standard residual decompositions and goodness-of-fit metrics when residual means deviate from zero.

candidates.title: Graphs in Statistical Analysis
candidates.reason: Influential pedagogical work demonstrating the necessity of transparently inspecting finite dataset prediction errors and residual patterns rather than assuming model adequacy from high-level summary statistics alone.

candidates.title: Partial Time Series Analysis
candidates.reason: Foundational work introducing the Frisch-Waugh theorem, demonstrating that sequential residual regression isolates partial linear relationships and showing the role of constant terms in de-meaning residual vectors.

candidates.title: Seasonal Adjustment of Economic Time Series and Multiple Regression Analysis
candidates.reason: Seminal formulation of the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell theorem, formally proving how orthogonal projections and intercept adjustments eliminate constant residual offsets across linear submodels.

candidates.title: Detection of Influential Observations in Linear Regression
candidates.reason: Seminal paper on regression diagnostics that establishes the formal framework for analyzing prediction residuals, demonstrating how omission of constant offsets uniformly shifts finite observation errors.

candidates.title: Greedy Function Approximation: A Gradient Boosting Machine
candidates.reason: Foundational predictive modeling paper establishing the formal paradigm where an initial constant prediction is determined by the mean target value, and subsequent residual calculations act as direct additive corrections.

candidates.title: Statistical Modeling: The Two Cultures
candidates.reason: Widely cited survey exploring prediction accuracy versus interpretability, emphasizing transparent finite-sample residual verification and the operational role of baseline predictors in statistical education.

candidates.title: Gauss and the Invention of Least Squares
candidates.reason: Foundational historical and mathematical investigation of Gauss's formulation of least squares, explaining the first-order conditions that force residual sums to zero in the presence of a constant intercept.

candidates.title: Scaling Regression Inputs by Dividing by Two Standard Deviations
candidates.reason: Influential pedagogical paper clarifying the direct interpretability of the regression intercept as the expected baseline outcome and analyzing how additive shifts in predictors and targets affect model constants.
